---
title: "About"
---

**Neuro Pattern Recognition (NPR)** is a companion for pattern recognition in core
neurocritical care diagnoses, built in the spirit of the Neurocritical Care Society's ENLS but
organized around a disease's *natural history* rather than the first hour of resuscitation.
Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage is the prototype module.

## Design

Two layers:

- **A deterministic engine** (`js/npr-*.js`) — a transparent time × system model of SAH natural
  history that runs entirely in the browser. It scores which complication domains dominate on a
  given day (rebleeding collapses once the aneurysm is secured; DCI is a skew-bell peaking day
  6–9, scaled by modified Fisher and IVH; hyponatremia salience jumps when the sodium is already
  low; and so on), then assembles the day's assessments, thresholds, pearls, and red flags from
  a matrix of timeline entries. It is auditable and works offline.
- **An AI tutor** — a guard-railed Claude model reached through a Firebase Cloud Function proxy
  (so no API key is ever in the browser), *fed the deterministic engine's brief as ground
  truth* plus a retrieved slice of the evidence cards. It gives Socratic feedback on a trainee's
  plan and answers focused questions. It is instructed to teach, not to order, and to name what
  to escalate and what to discuss with the team. The rest of the app works without it.

## Status

Prototype. **All clinical content is DRAFT** pending verification against primary sources —
see [Sources](sources.qmd). The reference specification (including a fuller design document and
an R implementation of the same engine) lives in a separate repository.

## Not a medical device

Educational use only. Not a substitute for attending or fellow supervision, institutional
protocols, or clinical judgment. Do not enter protected health information.
